summary: A is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the required convenience API, reuses multipartbody.NewFile, delegates to FilesService.Add, and avoids unrelated retry changes. B has stronger coverage in some areas but violates two explicit architectural and scope requirements.
reasons: A routes Upload through FilesService.Add, preserving centralized option handling, request construction, decoding, and error semantics exactly as required.
A reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field "file" and the supplied filename, making the encoded body replayable while propagating reader errors.
B duplicates the implementation of Add inside Upload instead of calling Add, creating maintenance drift and directly violating the contract.

B modifies RawClient retry and reader-ownership semantics, despite the explicit instruction not to refactor unrelated request/retry machinery. This broadens risk across all raw requests and Add/Update calls.
risks_a: Tests do not cover empty-filename and nil-content validation.
Tests do not exercise a source reader that returns an error.
The retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than a streamed/file-backed source and does not explicitly set RetryAllMethods, so it is less representative of the reported scenario.
risks_b: Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its option, request, response-decoding, and missing-data logic.
The RawClient change expands API semantics, including seeking behavior, content-length inference, and ownership/closing behavior, outside the requested scope.

The GetBody closure reuses and mutates one shared io.ReadSeeker, introducing coupling that is unnecessary when Upload already buffers through multipartbody.NewFile and may be fragile under other transport behavior or concurrent replay attempts despite passing current gates.
